newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PALMER FINDS STAYING AWAY FROM GOLF A TOUGH PRESCRIPTION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PALMER FINDS STAYING AWAY FROM GOLF A TOUGH PRESCRIPTION.

text.p: Golf legend Arnold Palmer said Friday he is finding it difficult to follow doctor's orders and stay away from golf after surgery for cancer.
"Not doing really very much of anything for 6 weeks is something ... that I haven't faced in years," said Palmer, who recently underwent surgery for prostate cancer.
"The last time I haven't swung a golf club in six weeks was about 1955. That is something that's going to be very difficult for me," Palmer told reporters at a news conference.
Palmer, 67, said he was feeling tired, but that his doctors said he was recovering well from the surgery.
Palmer won four Masters titles, two British Opens and one U.S. Open in his legendary career.
Credited with popularising the game in the television era, Palmer ranks fourth on the all-time PGA Tour victory list with 60 titles and has won 10 senior tournaments.
